item.title: (Weekly funding roundup Nov 7-14) VC inflow drops to its lowest level in 2026
item.description: The second week of November saw venture capital funding into Indian startups drop to its lowest level for the year till now due to weak deal activity.
item.content:encoded:
Weekly venture capital funding into Indian startups has dipped to the lowest level for the year till now due to a combination of the festive period and a lower number of deals.

The total venture capital funding for the second week of November was just $26 million from 11 deals. In comparison, the previous week saw a total amount of $263 million.

This is the lowest ever VC funding raised by Indian startups on a weekly basis for 2026. Prior to this, the lowest level was in the last week of May when the amount was $66 million.

This development reveals the challenges the Indian startup ecosystem continues to face in raising capital, amid the volatile macro economic environment.

The Indian startup ecosystem still greatly relies on overseas money. The increased trade tension among countries has curbed the flow of capital. However, the bigger challenge is the absence of a credible AI story in the country.

In the major VC ecosystems across the globe, it is the AI segment that has cornered the highest share of capital. This is particularly evident in the US where AI startups have raised a considerable amount of money.

In contrast, India has just a handful number of credible AI startups. This has been one of the key factors for the lower VC funding this year in the startup ecosystem.

The total VC funding for 2026 is unlikely to cross the level of 2025 given the current trends. In 2025, the Indian startup ecosystem raised $12.1 billion. The first ten months of 2026 saw VC funding of $10.4 billion, and the last two months may not see any significant VC activity.

item.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 16, 2026)
item.description: YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Monday, November 16, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
From Ola Electric making a major change to its retailing business, to India and US-based semiconductor company Bharat Semi raising $24 million in seed funding to develop programmable smart sensors, here are the latest developments across sectors.

Featured Stories

Ola Electric hands the keys to dealers. What led to this shift in gears?

On November 1, Ola Electric stopped taking orders at its own outlets. Most of them will be shut by December, as Ola moves away from the direct-to-consumer model that defined the company and turns to a dealer-led business.

Ola has recorded this in its investor presentation filed with the NSE and BSE on November 12 under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. The document covers the unaudited standalone and consolidated results for the second quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026.

In its Q2 FY27 shareholders' letter, dated November 12, the company calls the move towards a dealer-led model a "reset". What prompted this 'reset'?

Read more

Latest News

Oister Global launches Rs 600 Cr deeptech fund

Oister Global, an India-focused multi-strategy private markets asset manager, has announced the launch of a Rs 600 crore deeptech fund to back revenue generating Indian startups.

The Oister Deep Tech Fund aims to raise Rs 400 crore with a Rs 200 crore greenshoe, taking the potential corpus to Rs 600 crore.

A statement from Oister Global said this deeptech fund will build a concentrated portfolio of 8 to 10 mature companies in the frontier tech ecosystem. The fund will focus in sectors such as space technology, defence and aerospace, semiconductors and electronics, quantum technologies, advanced mobility, advanced materials and energy storage.

Read more

Funding News

Bharat Semi raises $24M to develop AI-enabled sensors

India- and US-based semiconductor company Bharat Semi has raised $24 million in seed funding to develop programmable smart sensors for Physical AI, where machines use artificial intelligence to perceive and act in the real world. 

The round was led by Info Edge, the internet group behind Naukri; South Park Commons, a founder community and early-stage investor; and IndusBridge Ventures, which backs deeptech sector. 

Micromax, an electronics group; Valour Capital, a deeptech investor; New York-based venture syndicate Gaingels and angel investors Mukul Agarwal and Kartik Iyer also participated.

Read more

Other News

Equity Intelligence invests Rs 2.5 crore in 90+ My Tuition App to launch Future+ Foundery

Equity Intelligence, the investment firm led by Porinju Veliyath, has invested Rs 2.5 crore in 90+ My Tuition App, owned by Daskalos Virtual Academy, at a Rs 50 crore valuation. The funds will launch Future+ Foundery, a separate brand offering school-integrated future-skills programmes. Its 15 learning areas include artificial intelligence, space technology, entrepreneurship, digital marketing, defence careers and leadership. 

Students begin with a Discovery Programme, then progress through Foundation, Advanced Learning and Real Industry Learning, each a one-year pathway. Proceeds will fund curriculum, school partnerships, technology and national expansion through a Future+ Integrated School Network, while Daskalos develops an AI Teacher Programme.

Arborum Labs raises pre-seed funding to build world models for complex networks

Bengaluru-based Arborum Labs has raised an undisclosed pre-seed round co-led by Speciale Invest and Ideaspring Capital to build AI world models for complex infrastructure networks. Other participants include BCG's Neeraj Aggarwal and Pranay Mehrotra and Sriram Rajamani, while ARTPARK and FSID are also supporters. 

Founded by IISc's Himanshu Tyagi and former BCG AI leader Pooja Rajdev, the startup models how power and telecom systems behave, supporting forecasting, trading, battery optimisation and outage detection. It already works with several Indian networks. The funds will accelerate development and expansion in India and the US, with a public version planned within a year.

Brighter Mind Category III AIF crosses Rs 50 crore in investor commitments

Brighter Mind Asset Management has crossed Rs 50 crore in investor commitments for its Category III AIF, Brighter Mind Inevitable Fortune Fund, launched in April 2025. The long-only fund focuses on listed Indian equities and the pre-IPO space, and uses no derivatives. 

Its investment approach rests on a proprietary 3M framework: Megatrend, Management and Margin of Safety. Led by founder, managing director and CEO CA Rajeev Ranjan and co-founder and CIO Manoj Bandre, the firm says the milestone reflects investor trust. It plans to stay disciplined in portfolio construction and remain committed to high-conviction, research-driven value investing as the fund grows.

mistEO raises Rs 18 crore seed round led by MGF-Kavachh to scale climate risk intelligence

Thiruvananthapuram-based climate intelligence company mistEO has raised Rs 18 crore in a seed round led by MGF-Kavachh, with Seafund and others participating. Announced at Huddle Global 2026, the funds will scale its Climate Decision Intelligence platform for banks, insurers and agri-value chains across India and Asia, deepen its forecasting models and grow its team. 

The platform fuses physics-based weather modelling with AI, using satellite, radar and sensor data to show how weather affects specific farms, assets or loans. Its Indra model forecasts at 3 km spatial resolution. mistEO already works with NABARD, UNDP, the Indian Air Force and Australian livestock farmers.

Consint.ai and Pramana HealthTech partner to drive connected health ecosystem across Asia-Pacific

Consint.ai, an Indian deep-tech company building foundational health AI models with IndiaAI Mission support, has signed a strategic partnership with Pramana HealthTech to explore opportunities across Asia-Pacific. The collaboration combines Consint.ai's generative and agentic AI capabilities with Pramana's ecosystem orchestration approach, aiming to connect financial, administrative, operational and clinical processes across payers, providers, pharmacies and laboratories. 

It will examine six areas, including financing models, claims and payer coordination, programme economics and outcome-based models, aligned with Pramana's Financial Orchestration for Healthcare Sustainability domain. Both firms intend to engage regional stakeholders, focusing on claims intelligence, financial integrity and process automation across programmes.""

Arborum Labs raises pre-seed round co-led by Speciale Invest and Ideaspring Capital

Arborum Labs, a Bengaluru-based AI startup building world models for complex networks, has raised an undisclosed pre-seed round co-led by Speciale Invest and Ideaspring Capital. Backers include BCG's Neeraj Aggarwal and Pranay Mehrotra, Sriram Rajamani, ARTPARK and early supporter FSID.

Co-founded by IISc's Himanshu Tyagi and former BCG generative AI leader Pooja Rajdev, the company's models learn how infrastructure components interact, helping operators simulate scenarios. In power, they support forecasting, trading and battery optimisation; in telecom, they detect impending outages. Arborum already works with several nationwide Indian networks and will use the funds to expand in India and the US.

Zoho Desk marks 10 years from Tenkasi and unveils Blended Agents for customer service

Zoho Desk, built in Tenkasi, Tamil Nadu, marks 10 years serving more than 125,000 businesses across 155 countries, growing roughly 35% annually between 2017 and 2025. To mark the anniversary, Zoho has launched Blended Agents, powered by Zia Agents, which retrieve information, execute tasks across connected applications and hand over to humans when judgement is needed.

Businesses can build and deploy AI agents at no extra cost, paying only for LLM usage. The release also adds Automation Studio, a customisable Workstation and WhatsApp calling and payments. Zoho's Tenkasi campus houses around 1,100 employees, about half of them local.

Uber partners with Mahindra Last Mile Mobility to support 5,000 electric autos

Uber has signed a memorandum of understanding with Mahindra Last Mile Mobility to support the adoption of 5,000 electric three-wheelers over the next 12 months. The EV Auto Advantage programme will offer drivers financing, trade-in incentives and support, focusing on markets where electric vehicle penetration remains low.

Announced in Mumbai on the sidelines of Earthshot Week, the partnership aims to make electric mobility a better economic choice for drivers. Uber also showcased Connected Journeys, a feature rolling out progressively from Delhi that combines autos or two-wheelers with metro travel in a single journey plan, with route options, timings and pricing visible in the app.

Medi Assist appoints Aruna Vaidyanathan as Chief Growth and Culture Officer

Medi Assist Healthcare Services has appointed Aruna Vaidyanathan, formerly Global Head of Growth Marketing at TCS, as Chief Growth and Culture Officer, reporting to CEO Satish Gidugu. She will build a unified go-to-market engine across its three businesses: Medi Assist Insurance TPA, India's largest third party administrator; its technology platforms; and Mayfair We Care, which administers international health benefits across 185 countries.

Her remit covers brand, market messaging and stakeholder communications, with each business given its own identity under one brand. She will also build a single culture across teams brought together through acquisitions and countries. She began her career as a business journalist.

Visage Lines launches rE, a recovery brand built around 10-minute daily resets

Visage Lines Personal Care, parent company of Bombay Shaving Company, has launched rE, a recovery brand built around 10-minute daily resets. The range has 14 products across three categories: Reset, Rewind and Recover, including a massage gun, foam roller, eye massager and calf sleeve.

Short routines target areas, such as three minutes for the neck and shoulders, five for the lower back and seven for the scalp and eyes. Routines were developed with orthopaedic surgeon Dr Manan Vora and physiotherapist Dr Yamini Burkule. The brand is pursuing partnerships with marathons, gyms and workplaces, and is available online from 16 November.

Quest Global acquires Tests Assured to strengthen wearables engineering and testing

Quest Global Engineering Services has acquired Tests Assured, a San Jose-based company specialising in quality assurance and technology-enabled testing for immersive products, smart devices and wearables. Founded in 2018, Tests Assured brings expertise in AR/VR/XR and smart-glasses testing, biometric validation, human-interaction modelling and computer-vision data collection, along with a strong presence among global wearable-device companies.

The acquisition aims to strengthen Quest Global's ability to deliver engineering solutions for wearables in the high-tech consumer space and support customers across the product lifecycle. The two companies will also pursue new opportunities in the hi-tech and semiconductor industries.

Recode Studios reports 24% revenue growth in H1 FY27

Beauty and personal care brand Recode Studios reported a 24% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations to Rs 45.82 crore for the first half of FY27, compared with Rs 36.91 crore in the corresponding period last year. Profit after tax increased 27% to Rs 4.92 crore, while EBITDA rose 9% to Rs 6.45 crore. The company attributed the performance to deeper market penetration and an expanding omnichannel distribution network.

Recode has expanded its retail presence to 25 franchise outlets, two company-owned stores and seven premium kiosks across more than 20 cities. It has also increased its portfolio to over 400 SKUs. The company expects to deliver more than 50% growth in FY27.

Scalar Field records $60 million in trading activity through AI agents

Y Combinator-backed fintech startup Scalar Field has recorded $60 million in cumulative trading activity through its AI trading agents, approximately four months after launching the platform in July 2026. The figure includes both simulated and live trading activity. The platform enables investors to develop trading strategies, test them against historical market data and deploy them through supported accounts.

Its AI capabilities assist with research and strategy development, while a separate execution system applies user-defined rules and monitors positions. Ramakant Yadav, Co-founder of Scalar Field, said the platform enables investors to translate market ideas into testable strategies without requiring dedicated research and engineering teams. The startup's next priority is improving transparency and helping users understand their agents' trading decisions.

Pensionbazaar partners Zypp Electric to offer NPS to gig workers

Pensionbazaar, a brand under Paisabazaar, has partnered with electric mobility platform Zypp Electric to offer National Pension System (NPS) solutions to its gig delivery partners. Zypp operates a fleet of more than 30,000 electric vehicles across eight cities and has impacted over 2.8 lakh gig workers. Under the partnership, eligible delivery partners can enrol in NPS through a digital, consent-based process and make contributions using UPI, net banking or cards.

Zypp aims to bring 60-70% of eligible delivery partners into the pension ecosystem within the first six to 12 months. The initiative seeks to address the limited access gig workers have to formal retirement benefits and encourage long-term savings through flexible contributions.

Fireflies.ai expands platform with AI teammate Fred

Fireflies.ai has expanded its product portfolio with the launch of Fred, an AI teammate designed to help organisations manage tasks across workplace applications. The platform brings together meeting notes, email, Slack, scheduling, screen recording and enterprise search. The company said Fred completed nearly 100 million tasks over the past six months, while usage beyond meeting notes grew 140%.

The expanded offering includes AI-powered meeting preparation, voice typing, email assistance, scheduling and voice agents. Fireflies also introduced Fireflies Fly, a hardware device designed to capture notes from phone calls and in-person conversations. The platform connects with over 240 tools. Fireflies said its new experience would roll out progressively, with paid plans starting at $10 per user per month.

Embark launches location analytics tool for GCC expansion in India

Embark has launched a Location Analytics Tool to help global companies identify suitable cities and micro-markets for establishing Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in India. The platform evaluates locations across seven parameters and more than 35 sub-parameters, covering talent availability, real estate, regulatory conditions, connectivity, infrastructure and liveability.

Companies can customise criteria based on their sector, proposed workforce and business functions. The tool also provides insights into peer GCCs, role-level talent availability and office rental costs. According to Embark, its database draws on research covering approximately 2,100 GCCs in India. The platform aims to simplify location selection, which traditionally involves extensive consultant-led studies, and enable companies to make faster, data-backed expansion decisions.

Kotak Mahindra Bank, NSRCEL onboard 90 women entrepreneurs under startup programme

Kotak Mahindra Bank, through its CSR initiative Kotak BizLabs, has onboarded 90 women entrepreneurs for the sixth cohort of its Women Startup Program (WSP 6), implemented in partnership with NSRCEL at IIM Bangalore. The seven-month hybrid incubation programme, running from September 2026 to April 2027, will help founders strengthen business models, improve customer acquisition, build brands and prepare for fundraising.

The programme is aimed at women founders who have developed a minimum viable product and begun engaging with customers or generating revenue. It combines online sessions with workshops, bootcamps and exhibitions. The initiative also provides mentorship, market access and investor-readiness support to help women-led businesses build sustainable enterprises.

Unstop launches AI bootcamp for students

Unstop has launched a Student AI Bootcamp, sponsored by Amazon Web Services (AWS), to provide students with opportunities to understand and explore artificial intelligence. The initiative aims to bridge the gap between classroom learning and practical exposure to emerging technologies.

Through its platform, Unstop will help students discover and participate in programmes focused on AI and its applications across sectors such as banking, healthcare, education and manufacturing.

NIELIT Hyderabad trains over 200 students in quantum technology

More than 200 students from nine educational institutions participated in a three-day workshop on quantum communications and applications in quantum technology organised by NIELIT Hyderabad under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.

Conducted from November 11 to 13 in partnership with QClairvoyance Quantum Labs, the workshop covered quantum mechanics, entanglement, quantum algorithms, quantum key distribution and post-quantum cryptography.

item.title: India, US have agreed on preferential market access for Indian goods in America: Piyush Goyal
item.description: India and the US finalised the framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement in February.
item.content:encoded:
India and the US have already agreed that Indian goods in the American market will receive preferential market access compared to competitor nations, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Sunday.

India and the US finalised the framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement in February.

The deal was to be signed earlier, but changes in the US tariff landscape have led to further negotiations on the agreement.

"This was already agreed between the leaders - President (Donald) Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi when they announced that we have both come to a broad framework agreement a few months ago and it has been acknowledged that India will get preferential trade access in the US with lower duties than our competitor countries," Goyal told reporters in Cairo.

He is here on a two-day visit to discuss ways to boost trade and investment between India and Egypt.

The minister was replying to a question about the US assurance that Indian goods will get preferential market access.

An official has recently stated that the US has assured India of a comparative tariff advantage over competing countries under the proposed bilateral trade agreement (BTA), with both sides working to conclude the first tranche by the end of the current financial year.

"We will have to see how the tariff framework unfolds. We are working towards closing the first tranche by the end of this financial year. Talks are going for the first tranche and the broader BTA," the official said last week.

The extent of the advantage to Indian goods, however, will depend on the tariff framework eventually agreed upon.

After the US Supreme Court struck down the Trump's reciprocal tariffs that were the basis of negotiations, the US is using alternate mechanisms to put up a new tariff architecture in place using provisions of the Trade Act.

item.title: Xpressbees raises Rs 100 Cr in debt from BlackSoil
item.description: Xpressbees has raised Rs 100 crore through secured, unlisted NCDs, at a 13.5% coupon over 36 months, to fund its working capital needs.
item.content:encoded:
Xpressbees, the Pune-based logistics company, has raised Rs 100 crore from alternative credit platform BlackSoil through the issue of non-convertible debentures (NCDs). The money will be used for the company's working capital needs.

The company's board approved the allotment on October 22, 2026. It issued 2,000 NCDs of Rs 5 lakh each through a private placement. BlackSoil Capital took 1,200 of them for Rs 60 crore, and BlackSoil India Credit Fund II took the remaining 800 for Rs 40 crore.

The debt carries an interest of 13.5% a year, paid monthly. It runs for 36 months, and the principal will be repaid in equal instalments. The documents also mention a second tranche, which suggests the money may come in more than one go.

The NCDs are backed by a claim on the company's assets, including cash flows, inventory and receivables, and excludes intellectual property. The promoters and directors are not putting in any money.

Xpressbees can repay early after 12 months. It will pay a 2% premium if it does so between months 13 and 17, and 1% between months 18 and 23. After 24 months, there is no premium.

Amitava Saha, Director and CEO of Busybees Logistics Solutions, certified the allotment on October 23, 2026. He is also authorised to file the required returns with the Registrar of Companies and to have the debentures credited to the investors' demat accounts.

Xpressbees was founded in 2015 as a spin-off from FirstCry by Amitava Saha and Supam Maheshwari. It is run by Busybees Logistics Solutions. The company offers B2C, B2B, cross-border and third-party logistics, and has a network of about 3,500 service centres and 150 hubs serving over 20,000 pin codes. Its clients include ecommerce players such as Snapdeal, Myntra, Meesho, Netmeds and BigBasket.

The company's revenue from operations grew marginally to Rs 2,874 crore in FY25 from Rs 2,831 crore in FY24, with courier services making up 96% of operating income. Net loss widened 85% to Rs 370 crore, and the EBITDA loss was Rs 228 crore. Total income was Rs 2,961 crore.

item.title: Bharat Semi raises $24M to develop AI-enabled sensors
item.description: Bharat Semi has raised seed funding to develop programmable AI-powered sensors, targeting the growing demand for intelligent, energy-efficient hardware for robotics, vehicles and other machines.
item.content:encoded:
India- and US-based semiconductor company Bharat Semi has raised $24 million in seed funding to develop programmable smart sensors for Physical AI, where machines use artificial intelligence to perceive and act in the real world. 

The round was led by Info Edge, the internet group behind Naukri; South Park Commons, a founder community and early-stage investor; and IndusBridge Ventures, which backs deeptech sector. 

Micromax, an electronics group; Valour Capital, a deeptech investor; New York-based venture syndicate Gaingels and angel investors Mukul Agarwal and Kartik Iyer also participated.

The funding will accelerate product development, expand the US engineering team and support efforts to secure global customers. 

Founded in 2021, Bharat Semi operates across New Delhi, Bengaluru and San Francisco. It is initially targeting consumer electronics and surveillance, with potential longer-term applications in robotics, vehicles, drones, aerospace and defence.

Its sensors combine data capture and AI processing in a single component. A camera-equipped device could interpret an image at the point of capture, rather than send raw data to a separate processor or cloud server. This is known as edge inference, where AI processes information close to its source, potentially reducing delays and energy consumption. 

Bharat Semi said its technology could reduce data movement between components by up to 99% and lower system costs by up to ten times compared with conventional multi-chip systems.

“Soon, growth in the sensor market will be driven by capturing data for machines,” co-founder Vinayak Dalmia said, arguing that sensing, processing and software must be designed together. 

Co-founder Vrinda Kapoor described the shift as “intelligence at the right place”, saying it offered India an opportunity to build globally relevant technology businesses. 

The technical team also includes Boyd Fowler, former chief technology officer of image-sensor maker OmniVision.

The investment comes as AI moves beyond data centres and into physical devices and machines. Bharat Semi has reportedly secured design wins with US defence company General Atomics and India's Kaynes Semicon.

Other Indian deeptech ventures have attracted funding this year. Bengaluru-based chipmaker C2i Semiconductors raised $15 million in February, while sensor and navigation technology developer Yaanendriya secured Rs 15 crore in July. Physical AI startup Flo Mobility raised $2.5 million in May to expand its construction robotics business.

Policy support is also expanding. Approved in July 2026 with an outlay of Rs 1,27,500 crore, India’s Semicon 2.0 programme covers chip design, manufacturing equipment and materials, fabrication, packaging, research and talent development. In November, the government reported that five of 12 approved semiconductor projects had commenced commercial production.

item.title: How Tej Chingtham built Northeast’s first incubator; The pilot-turned-entrepreneur who is building a wellness brand
item.description: In a conversation with Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project, Prof Tej Chingtham, CEO of Atal Incubation Centre - Sikkim Manipal University Technology Business Incubation Foundation, recalls what led him to look at the Northeast's startup ecosystem closely.
item.content:encoded:
Dear Reader,

How should AI be measured? Should the focus be on the number of agents deployed?

Natalia Rachelson, Senior Vice President, Applications Development, Oracle, believes the number of agents matters less than the improvement they deliver. She says business leaders should pick outcomes they can measure, such as reducing time spent resolving accounting errors or lowering transport costs. 

While impact matters, so does responsible usage. 

India’s markets regulator Sebi will soon issue detailed guidelines for responsible use of AI in the capital markets. 

Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the proposed guidelines would focus on establishing appropriate guardrails for AI use, including disclosures, accountability of regulated entities, and a ‘human-in-the-loop’ approach. 

Moving on, Zomato-parent Eternal is reassessing its 2030 target for a 100% electric delivery fleet due to rapid business expansion and an evolving EV ecosystem.

Anjalli Ravi Kumar, Chief Sustainability Officer at Eternal, said the company is working towards a revised timeline, factoring in availability of electric vehicles, supporting government policies, and the transportation requirements of its various businesses.

In other news, India and the US have already agreed that Indian goods in the American market will receive preferential market access compared to competitor nations, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal told media in Cairo. India and the US finalised the framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement in February. 

ICYMI: Here’s the video of SpaceX’s Starship’s incredible return to the launch pad from orbit.

In today’s newsletter, we will talk about 

  • How Tej Chingtham built Northeast’s first incubator
  • The pilot-turned-entrepreneur who is building a wellness brand 

Here’s your trivia for today: What is the rare economic condition when rising prices and recession occur at once? (Scroll down for the answer)

Startup Ecosystem

How Tej Chingtham built Northeast’s first incubator

When young people from Northeast India approached Prof (Dr) Tej Chingtham with questions about starting a business, he did not always have the answers. In a conversation with Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project, Dr Chingtham recalled how these interactions prompted him to look more closely at the region’s startup ecosystem in 2016.

What began as an attempt to understand the challenges that local entrepreneurs faced eventually led him to build an incubation centre. He battled stage III lung cancer while working towards the centre’s establishment. Today, he is the CEO of the Atal Incubation Centre - Sikkim Manipal University Technology Business Incubation Foundation, which works with more than 200 startups. The wider Northeast ecosystem has grown to over 2,000 startups. 

Key takeaways 

  • Dr Tej Chingtham believes the Northeast needs more startups relative to its population. Reaching that point will require sustained mentorship, supportive policies, and investors willing to explore opportunities beyond established markets.
  • Dr Chingtham’s ambition was never limited to setting up an incubation centre in Sikkim. He wanted entrepreneurs across the Northeast to have access to the mentorship and support that were often easier to find in established startup hubs.
  • He wants more young people to consider entrepreneurship as a viable career and use the resources available in their own states to build businesses at home. Rather than viewing the Northeast as a place to leave in search of employment, he wants youngsters to see it as a place where businesses can grow.

Inspiration

This pilot-turned-entrepreneur is building a wellness brand for women

After a decade flying for IndiGo, Natasha Chaudhary turned to her own experiences with hormonal changes to launch Everyday You, a wellness brand for women navigating the health concerns that come with middle age. The brand has been built on the premise that women don’t have to suffer through it.

Key takeaways

  • Everyday You blends Ayurveda and modern science, bringing together ingredients such as magnesium, ashwagandha, chasteberry and shatavari in a single formulation. 
  • The brand has launched two products so far. Everyday Balance is a hormonal wellness blend that targets mood, anxiety, sleep, and night sweats. The second product, Everyday De-Bloat, is a natural solution for post-meal bloating, indigestion, and period bloat. 
  • In the crowded market of nutraceuticals riding on rising awareness around perimenopause and menopause, Natasha is betting on a more cautious message: women do not need everything on the shelf. “I’m putting myself out there and saying that what helped me can help you as well,” she says.

News & updates

  • US-China talks: US President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping this week with a key part ​of his trade strategy unfinished: securing a homegrown supply of critical minerals to counter Beijing’s dominance. China is expected to use its dominance in rare earths as a negotiating tool.
  • Ageing systems: A massive, nearly five-hour shutdown of the US aviation system that has disrupted more than 20,000 flights since Friday may have been the fault of a single router installed by government contractor L3Harris, government officials said. The incident is the latest example of the ageing US air traffic control telecom system ​and the struggles to replace systems while keeping the old communications working. 
  • Alice Huang: Megaspeed has said that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whose ties ​to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have raised US national ‌security concerns, officially left the company on August 30, 2025, and has no current role there. 

What you should watch out for

Bengaluru Tech Summit: The 29th edition of the Bengaluru Tech Summit runs from November 17 to 19 at BIEC under the theme ‘AI & Beyond’, bringing together the global technology ecosystem to explore AI and the breakthrough technologies shaping the future. 

What is the rare economic condition when rising prices and recession occur at once?

item.title: India’s deeptech funding record faces a test of scale: Speciale Invest report
item.description: India’s deeptech funding hit $914 million in 2025, but limited growth capital, manufacturing dependencies and weak commercialisation pathways continue to hinder startups from scaling.
item.content:encoded:
India’s deeptech companies raised $914 million in 257 rounds in 2025, 34 times the 2016 level. The harder test is turning research and prototypes into commercial products, notes Speciale Invest’s report, India’s Deep Tech Revolution - From the Lab to Growth and Exits.

Using Tracxn data through August 31 2026, the study covers 8,293 private companies worldwide, including 482 in India. India accounted for 12.8% of deeptech funding rounds in 2025 but received 1.6% of the capital. 

For every 100 seed rounds, India had 23 Series A or B rounds, against 105 globally. Separately, there was one late-stage or private-equity round per 100 Indian seed rounds, against 26 worldwide. Both measures point to funding thinning as companies mature.

Sectoral advantages are uneven. Space firms can tap ISRO testing facilities and suppliers, while life-sciences ventures can draw on India’s pharmaceutical manufacturing base. Private participation in space has widened since 2020 reforms. Registered space startups rose from one in 2014 to about 440 by August 2026. 

In July, Skyroot’s Vikram-I became the first privately developed Indian rocket to reach orbit from Indian soil. It was a milestone, though one launch does not establish a repeatable commercial business. 

The report says battery makers still rely on imported cells and materials. Separately, Exide commissioned phase one of a 6 GWh Bengaluru cell plant in September. Semiconductor developers remain reliant on overseas fabrication and packaging. Semicon 2.0, approved in July with Rs 1,27,500 crore, aims to expand domestic capacity; the first fab is due in 2028.

The six-year Rs 1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation Scheme aims to finance high-risk technology. By July 2026, the Technology Development Board had approved 22 projects with Rs 2,192 crore in support. Assistance is mainly through low-interest long-term loans, equity and equity-linked instruments, rather than standard grants.

Turning a successful pilot, or customer trial, into an order remains difficult. Vishesh Rajaram, managing partner at Speciale Invest, said, “Large companies and public-sector buyers can help turn those trials into commercial orders by agreeing upfront on what a pilot must prove and when they’ll make a purchase decision. A first order lets a startup plan production and commit to suppliers.”

Growth capital is smaller too. Indian Series A and B rounds averaged $11.5 million from January to August 2026, against $55.5 million globally, said Vishnu Rajeev, investment partner at Speciale Invest. 

“That gap matters when a founder needs to qualify a product with a major customer or commission a production line before commercial revenue is predictable, Rajeev adds. He argues funding should match milestone costs, with project finance once customers make firm commitments.

The report urges faster funding decisions, shared testing facilities, more domestic Series B and C investors, and plant finance before pilots end. It also considers listings, acquisitions, licensing and secondary share sales as exit routes. 

Deeptech needs not just research funding, but reliable customers and patient growth capital.
